issues.title: Type mismatch in blocks_variable_output prevents variable blocking
issues.description: The blocks_variable_output method compares a Sequence (assigned_variable_selector) directly against a set of tuples (variable_selectors), but fails to convert the Sequence to a tuple first. This type mismatch causes the 'in' check to always return False, meaning the Variable Assigner node will never properly block streaming output of conversation variables. As a result, the response coordinator will incorrectly allow streaming to proceed before conversation variables are updated, violating the intended synchronization logic and potentially showing stale variable values to users.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
def blocks_variable_output(self, variable_selectors: Set[Tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:
    """
    Check if this Variable Assigner node blocks the output of specific variables.

    Returns True if this node updates any of the requested conversation variables.
    """
    assigned_selector = self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector
    return assigned_selector in variable_selectors

issues.title: Incorrect input value used in NodeRunResult for CLEAR mode
issues.description: The code attempts to use updated_variable.to_object() for the CLEAR write mode's input value, but this represents the final cleared state rather than the input that triggered the operation. In CLEAR mode, income_value is actually the zero value generated by SegmentType.get_zero_value(), which is what should be shown as the input. This causes the NodeRunResult to misrepresent what value was used as input to the clear operation, breaking observability and potentially confusing downstream systems that rely on accurate input tracking.

issues.title: Test uses list equality instead of tuple conversion for event selector
issues.description: The test compares event.selector (which is a Sequence[str]) with a list literal using ==. While this might work in some cases due to Python's sequence equality, it's fragile and inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase. The original code correctly converted to tuple for comparison (tuple(event.selector) == ('conversation', 'conv_var')). This change breaks the filtering logic and will likely cause the test to fail to properly identify conversation variable chunk events, leading to false test failures.

]

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30832 - fix(api): defer streaming response until referenced variables are updated
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds a `blocks_variable_output` override to the v1 Variable Assigner node so the response stream coordinator waits for a conversation-variable write before streaming dependent Answer nodes. It also adds a v1 fixture workflow and an end-to-end streaming test. The intent and root-cause analysis are sound, and the new test is a real regression guard: it fails on the base code because the streamed chunk value is wrong.

The implementation is broken, though. The override checks `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector` (a `Sequence[str]`, which pydantic materializes as a `list`) directly against a `set` of tuples. Python raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`, and the coordinator calls this method from `register()` for every response node whose path runs through the assigner. I ran the PR's test file: the new test fails with that exact TypeError. Running the base code instead, the same test fails on the chunk-value assertion, so the test is valid and the override is the defect. Converting the selector to a tuple makes both tests pass.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new v1 `blocks_variable_output` raises an unhandled TypeError for every v1 Variable Assigner on a path to a response node with variable segments. That is the exact workflow shape this PR targets, so it is a regression (those workflows worked before and now crash), and the PR's own test fails. The fix is a one-line tuple conversion, which I verified, so this should be fixed before merge. The remaining findings are minor cleanup.

architecture.overview:
Dify's advanced-chat workflow engine runs nodes concurrently and streams Answer node output to the client. The `ResponseStreamCoordinator` (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine/response_coordinator/coordinator.py`) decides when a response node may start streaming. On `register()` it builds a paths map: for each root-to-response path it keeps only edges whose source node is a BRANCH, CONTAINER, or RESPONSE node, or whose `blocks_variable_output(...)` returns True for the variables referenced in the response template. The base `Node` returns False, and only nodes that write variables override it (the v2 Variable Assigner already does, by checking each item's selector as a tuple).

The PR adds the same override to the v1 `VariableAssignerNode`, so a v1 assignment to a conversation variable that an Answer references now holds streaming until the assignment completes. The PR also normalises the v1 result's `inputs['value']` for CLEAR mode, which is behaviour-neutral. The override's selector comparison is where the change goes wrong, because the v1 selector is a list and the coordinator's set holds tuples.
steps: Entry point: the graph engine calls `ResponseStreamCoordinator.register(response_node_id)` when it starts a response (Answer) node (`graph_engine.py`, `_start_execution`).
`register()` calls `_build_paths_map`, which collects the variable selectors from the response template as tuples (`coordinator.py` lines ~172-175) and walks every root-to-response path.
For each executable node on a path, the coordinator calls `source_node.blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors)` (`coordinator.py` line ~220). Only nodes that override this method can block.

The PR's change: `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` in `variable_assigner/v1/node.py` (lines 36-43) now overrides the base no-op. This is the step that needs a fix. The selector must be converted to a tuple before the set-membership check, matching the v2 override.
The PR also changes the v1 `_run` result: the CLEAR branch now reports `updated_variable.to_object()` instead of the zero-value object (lines 102-106). The value is the same either way.

Test coverage: a new v1 fixture (Start → Variable Assigner → Answer referencing `conversation.conv_var`) and a test that asserts all streamed `conversation.conv_var` chunks equal the input query. This test exercises the full path through `register()`.

findings.title: v1 blocks_variable_output raises TypeError on list selector, crashing streaming
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, `VariableAssignerNode.blocks_variable_output` (lines 36-43) compares `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector` directly against a set of tuples. Pydantic types that field as `Sequence[str]` and produces a `list`, so `in` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` whenever `ResponseStreamCoordinator._build_paths_map` (`coordinator.py` ~line 220) reaches this node. Convert the selector to a tuple before the membership check, following the v2 override in `variable_assigner/v2/node.py`. Also normalise to the first two segments the way `coordinator.py` ~line 175 does (`tuple(selector[:2])`), so the two sides match by construction. Then run `test_streaming_conversation_variables_v1_overwrite_waits_for_assignment` in `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/test_streaming_conversation_variables.py`, which currently fails with this TypeError.

findings.title: Unrelated CLEAR-mode inputs change with no test or stated reason
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py` `_run` (lines ~102-112), the PR added a `result_input_value` branch so CLEAR mode reports `updated_variable.to_object()`. That is behaviour-equivalent to the original `income_value.to_object()`, because the CLEAR branch sets `updated_variable` to that same zero value, and the change is unrelated to the streaming fix. Revert to the original `inputs={"value": income_value.to_object()}` and remove the new branch, unless you can show a behavioural difference and add a test for it.

findings.title: Typing imports diverge from the codebase's builtin generic style
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, line 2 imports `Set` and `Tuple` from `typing`, and line 36 annotates with `Set[Tuple[str, ...]]`. Switch to builtin generics to match `base/node.py` (line 435) and `variable_assigner/v2/node.py` (line 70): use `set[tuple[str, ...]]` and drop `Set`/`Tuple` from the import. Keep `TYPE_CHECKING` and `Any`.

findings.title: Regression test reproduces the original race and is well scoped
findings.body:
The new end-to-end test uses a v1 fixture where Start → Variable Assigner → Answer references `conversation.conv_var`. It checks both the final answer and that every streamed `conversation.conv_var` chunk equals the query. I verified that this test fails on the base code, with the chunk-value assertion. So it detects the race that the PR targets, rather than passing trivially. The one defect in the test's coverage is that it only passes with the TypeError fixed, which is the defect in the implementation, not in the test.

::code{file="api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/test_streaming_conversation_variables.py" lines="50-75"}

findings.title: Root-cause analysis matches the engine's blocking model
findings.body:
The PR description says the v1 assigner doesn't override `blocks_variable_output`, so the coordinator treats it as non-blocking. I checked this against `coordinator.py` and it holds: only overriding nodes can contribute blocking edges, and the base implementation returns False. The override's contract ("does this node write any requested conversation variable") is the right one, and the v1 override is scoped to the single selector it writes. Once the selector is converted to a tuple, it mirrors the v2 design.

::file{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/base/node.py"}
